purpose: Wave 39's route card for CT42's socket arm. One case NEWLY MAPPED (CT42) on the `sequential` route (the harness's name for the non-concurrent source routes; the artifact is a `source.socket.v1` program), under the `reject` verdict mode: the case asks the disjointness question of the two ends of one accepted connection and is refused by the unedited DisjointFootprintsV1 checker as SharedProtocolCell (Q664). Mapped stays a grown denominator: 46 -> 47 of 50 is mapping, not conformance (constraint 23).
derivation_rule: Every `verified_stages` block below is the manifest's own row for that case, which `compiler/tests/ct_corpus.rs` independently rederives from its own dispatch and refuses drift on. Nothing here is a second hand-kept copy.
why_this_case_maps_now: Card CT42-PROTOCOL-CELL (wave 31) derived the protocol cell at model level and card CT-CTWIN-LANE (wave 35) measured the arm UNROUTED: derive_socket_cells and footprint_program were called from one unit test and from nothing in the frontend, the checker or compile_files, so no .qcore program could reach Q664 and a CT row would have named a stage the harness cannot execute (CT42-CELL-UNROUTED). This card routes the deriver from source: `disjoint NAME NAME;` on source.socket.v1 (one reserved word, census-clean at zero QCore source occurrences), the transport checker deciding only that both names are live sockets of the entry, and qcore_core::socket_footprint::check_socket_cells handing one DeriveDescriptorAlias per socket plus one AssertDisjoint per question to the unedited footprint checker. compile_files now reaches Q664 on the case's own fixture, which is exactly what constraint 23's `executed only where a named workspace test runs it on the case's own artifact` requires. Before routing, the two admitting fallback arms of the deriver (CT42-CELL-FALLBACK-ARM-DIRECTION) were made refusals, each shown reachable by a fixture that drives the walk directly, and the T09 checker gained the derived-alias event so a derived-cell certificate carries no DeclaredProtocolCellIdentity (CT42-CELL-DERIVED-PREMISE).
attribution: The case's Q664 is attributed to the `disjoint client server;` statement (the harness pins the line source), under the Concurrency pass, which owns the Q650-Q667 band. The refusal message names both custodians and the cell. Five controls isolate it: a question over the listener and an end (admitted, and it emits the case's C byte for byte because the question erases), the ends of two different connections (admitted), a datagram pair (admitted; CT42-CELL-UDP-QUEUE re-affirmed with its ground), a question of a closed custodian (refused Q083 then Q082 by the inherited ownership and transport checkers, before any cell is derived), and a question naming a scalar (the transport checker's Q081).

boundaries_published_not_papered_over.two_descriptors: The two names are two descriptor slots of one program on one thread, the connector and the accepted binding of one completed TCP connection. No dup-like alias over one open description exists on any route (CT42-CELL-DUP-SOURCE, left open), so the scenario word `descriptors` is carried by the connection-cell reading, not the dup reading.
boundaries_published_not_papered_over.shared_logical_state: Read off the transport checker's own cross-name rules (a send through one end is decided by the other's committed stream; a close of one is refused while the other's bytes sit unread). Those rules are the transport checker's measured behaviour and the derivation's documented ground; the Lean model of this card proves the DERIVATION (an accepted pair shares one cell, a fresh cell is no existing cell, the unpaired arms refuse) and the assumption narrowing, not a theorem that the transport model's coupling is the shared state (SOCKET-CELL-COUPLING-UNPROVED, registered).
boundaries_published_not_papered_over.native_stage: The case is a refusal that emits nothing, so no native stage exists for the case's own artifact; the accepted controls emit C but no runner of this harness compiles or runs a sequential_reject control, so nothing is claimed for them. The C-twin arm (legacy_c_twin) stays blocked: the contract loader refuses an int-typed resource identity, and a descriptor's -1 failure value is not expressible in qcore-schemas' ResourceReturnMode (CT-CTWIN-DESCRIPTOR); that is out of this card's scope and stays unassessed in prose, not_applicable structurally on this route.
